sections.text:

devisedanartificialintelligencetechniqueonthebasisofdeepconvolutionalneuralnetworkfordiscoveringCOVID-19patientswithreal-world
databases. The system attained chest x-ray images for identifying the patients. The findings represent that this kind of assessment was benefi-
cial for COVID-19 diagnosis. However, the techniques failed to consider other parameters, like humidity, temperature, and terrain. In addition,
the time consumption was very high. Marco-Franco et al.9 developed a scheme for COVID-19 that incorporates data based on mortality rate.
The prediction of casualties in Spain, and the infectious-case fatality rate (IFR) and case fatality rate (CFR) for outbreak were evaluated. How-
ever,thetechniquefailedtoinvolveage-relatedfatalityratio.Kumar 24 developedaclusterassessmentbasedondataminingforclassifyingareal

times generated error values. James and Menzies25 devised an assessment that resulted to cluster countries based on active cases with Johns

Hopkins epidemiological data. The obtained result of the cluster was helpful for various policy makers like managers and physicians. In addi-
tion,theclusteringtechniquewasadaptedforcomparingseveralCOVIDtime-seriesdata.However,thistechniquefailedtodealwithreal-world
applications. Villanustre et al.6 developed a technique for analyzing the COVID-19 patient data. This method helped among several domains,
like healthcare, medical, and public applications. The developed technique handled the solutions for solving public health issues. However, the
consumption of time was high. Zoabi et al.26 developed a machine learning technique, which trained records using 51,831 tested individuals.
The test ser comprises data among the consequent week. The model helped to predict COVID-19 test results with elevated accuracy con-
sidering binary features. The method can be utilized among other considerations for prioritizing testing of COVID-19, while testing resources
were less. However, this technique failed to generate improved outcomes. Prinja et al.27 designed susceptible-exposed-infectious-recovered
(SEIR) for predicting the health results using an unmitigated scenario that consists of air travel restrictions, and the present case consist of
air travel restrictions among 8-week lockdown. Moreover, the technique computed the efficiency of lockdown. The computational complex-
ity of this model was high. Zubair et al.
14 developed an effective K-means clustering technique that discovered the initial centroids in an
effective manner. The technique helped to discover the quality of health care using COVID-19 databases. The technique showed that the
model reduced the count of iterations and time of execution for analyzing COVID-19. However, this technique failed to process with large
instances.

sections.title: 3.1 FeatureselectioninslavenodesusingproposedPRDOAalgorithm
sections.text:
The feature selection offers a way to reduce the time of computation, enhance performance and offer an improved understanding of data. In
addition, the feature selection is effective in making the data suitable for further processing. The goal of feature selection is building a simple
and comprehensible model with clean and understandable data. Moreover, the feature selection process is considered as an imperative step to
speed up learning and enhance the quality of data. Here, the feature selection is done using the proposed PRDOA algorithm, which is obtained
by combining PRO28 and DE29 algorithms. The solution encoding, and fitness function steps of the proposed PRDOA algorithm are described
below.

acceptable solutions to real-world issues. This algorithm converges with few functions, and is capable to address several engineering problems.

phins that perform hunting. The DE works based on computational effort in which the user affords for optimization. Here, the DE provides a
suitable convergence factor based on the problem. The DE provides the optimum answer in the count of loops offered by the user. The com-
bination of PRO and DE helps to enhance overall performance with global optimal solution. The steps involved in the proposed PRDOA are
